_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::ehl#2, and a FALSIFICATION of both halves of its Signal. The entry said Picard iteration 'diverges or oscillates between two states' and told the reader to apply Aitken or fixed under-relaxation. On upstream ehl_bearing_barus.4C.yaml, multiplying MAT_lubrication_law_barus/PreVisCoeff by 100 does not oscillate: the Newton residual goes 5.33839e+01 -> 7.95637e+70 in one step and the process is killed by SIGFPE, 'Signal code: Floating point divide-by-zero (3)', inside LubricationEleCalc::calc_mat_psl. The shell sees 136; 4C prints no error line, no 'did not converge' and no result-test verdict, because MPI_Abort is never reached. And the recommended relaxation is inert: MAXOMEGA/MINOMEGA/STARTOMEGA live in ELASTO HYDRO DYNAMIC/PARTITIONED, consulted only when COUPALGO is ehl_IterStagg, while the default is ehl_Monolithic — the RELAX arm dies identically with no notice that the keys were ignored. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C (2026.2.0-dev, commit 89519cfe76).

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: keep the upstream pressure-viscosity coefficient in both bad arms. Both then run to completion, EXIT_BIGALPHA/EXIT_RELAX stop being 136, the SIGFPE lines vanish and the fixture must go red.

remove the inert-relaxation half: stop injecting the omega keys. RELAX_ARM_HAS_OMEGA_KEYS drops to 0, so the claim that the recommended relaxation was actually requested and still did nothing is no longer demonstrated and the fixture must go red.
